channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Parent and child – Termination – Reasonable efforts
item.description: Where a mother’s parental rights were terminated by a Juvenile Court judge, the termination decree should be affirmed because the mother has waived her argument that the judge erred in ruling that the Department of Children and Families made reasonable efforts to prevent or eliminate the need for removal from the home.

item.title: Municipal – Opioids – Public nuisance
item.description: Where the city of Boston brought suit alleging that two pharmacy benefit managers violated Massachusetts public nuisance law by colluding with opioid manufacturers to misrepresent the risks of such drugs, the dismissal of the public nuisance claim as time-barred should be affirmed because the lower court committed no error in holding that the claim was not tolled under G.L.c. 260, §12

item.title: Education – Corporal punishment
item.description: Where a substantive due process claim has been brought against a defendant teacher, his motion to dismiss on qualified immunity grounds should be denied because the complaint adequately pleads a conscience-shocking violation of the plaintiff student’s right to be free from excessive corporal punishment, a right that was clearly established at the time of the teacher’s alleged misconduct.

item.title: Immigration – Employment authorization
item.description: Where two plaintiffs, one of whom is a Venezuelan national living and working in Massachusetts on a valid H-1B visa, have filed an emergency motion for preliminary injunction requiring adjudication of a pending application for employment authorization, their motion should be allowed because they are likely to succeed on their claim that the Department of Homeland Security’s two policy memoranda (PM-602-0192 and PM-602-0194) imposing a hold on adjudicating applications are arbitrary and capriciou

item.title: Models who sued over use of images denied coverage
item.description: A federal judge ruled that an intellectual property exclusion in a CGL policy barred coverage for Massachusetts strip clubs sued over unauthorized use of professional models’ images.

item.title: SJC justice rejects DiZoglio’s bid for representation in legislative audit case
item.description: Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court justice denies Auditor Diana DiZoglio's motion to appoint special counsel in her bid to audit the state Legislature.

item.title: New York sues video game developer Valve, says its ‘loot boxes’ are gambling
item.description: New York's attorney general sued Valve, accusing its loot boxes of illegal gambling and risking addiction among children. The lawsuit demands fines and restitution.

item.title: Worcester pastor accused of fraud ordered into involuntary bankruptcy
item.description: A federal judge has forced a longtime Worcester pastor the state is pursuing for alleged fraud into involuntary bankruptcy.

item.title: Insurance – Cost-of-living adjustment – Disability income policy
item.description: Where a defendant insurance company issued a disability income policy to the plaintiff, a judgment in favor of the plaintiff should be reversed because the policy language establishes that the cost-of-living adjustment increases stop on the policy anniversary after an insured has turned 65.

item.title: DOJ abandons defense of orders targeting law firms
item.description: The DOJ has abandoned its appeals defending Trump’s executive orders targeting law firms, allowing sanctions to remain blocked by judges.
